# Process — the rules in force

Loaded with `/scope`, `/step`, `/steps`, `/ship`, `/new-adr`, `/bootstrap` and any review pass. Each line names the record it comes from; open that record when the line is not enough. Which windows are open and which records are in force is stated once, in [the ledger](../plan/README.md#the-window).

- **Deliverables** — Work is staged into numbered deliverables, one plan file each, steps written `D<n>.<step>`, and each closes on an executable acceptance checklist. More than one may be in progress when no record — written, superseded or amended in place — belongs to two of them; each is a lane, and the condition is checked by a test when a lane opens. At most one open lane adds migrations. Steps stay sequential within a lane. — [ADR-0079](../adr/0079-parallel-lanes.md) (parallel lanes) as carried by [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md), [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-deliverables.md) (deliverables) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0079](../adr/0079-parallel-lanes.md)
- **The window** — An ADR may be amended in place only while the deliverable it belongs to is in progress; once that deliverable ships the record changes only by supersession, and opening a second lane reopens nothing. Which windows are open, and which records are in force, is stated in one place — the ledger's window section, which links one file per open lane — and linked from everywhere else. — [ADR-0079](../adr/0079-parallel-lanes.md) (parallel lanes) as carried by [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md), [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-deliverables.md) (deliverables) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0079](../adr/0079-parallel-lanes.md)
- **Lane files and tiers** — Each open lane is a file, `docs/plan/lanes/D<n>.md`: the deliverable and its plan, the date it opened, its branch, its tier, whether it adds migrations, and its records. `/scope` creates it when a lane opens and `/ship` removes it. The window section's list of lanes and its running paragraph are generated from the files by `pnpm lanes`, never edited by hand, and a conflict in them is resolved by running it; the paragraph states only what the files say, and a window's history is the ledger's `How D<n> opened` and `How D<n> closed` sections. A plan's header names its tier beside `- Schema:` — `package` needs no Postgres beyond a harness's own tests and no SPA build, `api` takes a lane database, `schema` is the one lane that adds migrations; the tier declares what a lane expects to need, and the step check still sizes itself to the diff — and `pnpm docs:check` refuses a lane whose tier its plan does not name, and a stale generated block. — [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) (lanes on one machine and one `main`) as carried by [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md), [ADR-0079](../adr/0079-parallel-lanes.md) (parallel lanes) as carried by [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md)
- **Lanes** — Every lane builds on a branch of its own from its first step — `lane/D<n>`, or the branch a cloud session was given, as its lane file names — with one draft pull request to `main`. A step is one commit pushed to it: it begins by reading the last push's `gate.yml` run and fixes forward when that is red, or says in its note that it could not read it; it ends on the step check and one review; it never merges to `main` and never waits on CI. `main` is merged into a lane only when the lane needs something `main` has or GitHub reports a conflict, and a conflicted generated file is regenerated, never hand-merged. `main` takes the documents-only commits `/scope` writes — the scoping, a lane's opening — and each lane once, when `/ship`, on the lane's head, merges its pull request with a merge commit and tags the merge commit. Deliverable and record numbers are reserved by scoping on `main`. `/step`, `/steps` and `/ship` take the deliverable while more than one row is in progress and refuse a bare call then. — [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) (lanes on one machine and one `main`) as carried by [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md), [ADR-0079](../adr/0079-parallel-lanes.md) (parallel lanes) as carried by [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md)
- **Acceptance at the head** — A record written `proposed` is accepted at the head of the step that builds it, so a step whose record is still `proposed` is gated and must not be started. — [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-deliverables.md) (deliverables) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0079](../adr/0079-parallel-lanes.md)
- **Supersession states the delta** — A superseding record states the delta and carries the parent's untouched sections by reference; whole restatement is permitted and never required. Where a supersession is a delta the parent still stands for everything the successor does not touch. — [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-adr-lifecycle-and-verification.md) (ADR lifecycle v2) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md)
- **Altitude** — A record decides; it does not enumerate. Counts, rosters and anything a compiler could check belong in tests and lint rules rather than in prose. — [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-adr-lifecycle-and-verification.md) (ADR lifecycle v2) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md)
- **Verification** — Machines are the gate; review is one bounded pass over the diff per step, in a fresh context — no refutation rounds and no zero-finding requirement. Where the builder cannot run a reviewer, the orchestrating session's pass is that one review; the builder's own reading is not a review. A deliverable has no close-out step: its last step builds, and `/ship` runs the definition of done — `pnpm docs:check` refuses a close-out step in a plan dated after the record withdrew them. Uncertain mechanics get a timeboxed spike in a worktree rather than a debate. — [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-adr-lifecycle-and-verification.md) (ADR lifecycle v2) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md), [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) (lanes on one machine and one `main`) as carried by [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md)
- **The gate** — The gate command is defined once, in `CLAUDE.md` §Commands, and referenced by name everywhere else. `pnpm check` is the cached inner loop; a task whose result depends on anything outside the repository is never cached and declares its `env`. A cached task's hash covers every workspace whose source it runs: `test:unit` reaches its workspace dependencies through turbo's `transit` node, which no workspace defines as a script. — [ADR-0026](../adr/0026-task-graph-caching-and-serialisation.md) (turborepo task graph) as carried by [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-grid-and-admin-followups.md) and [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md), [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-grid-and-admin-followups.md) (grid and admin follow-ups) as carried by [ADR-0054](../adr/0054-design-language-instrument.md) and [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-impersonation-sessions.md) and [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-frontend-build-and-shared-composition.md) and [ADR-0080](../adr/0080-interface-polish.md), [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-impersonation-sessions.md) (impersonation sessions) as carried by [ADR-0067](../adr/0067-organizations.md) and [ADR-0070](../adr/0070-impersonation-in-a-new-tab.md) and [ADR-0071](../adr/0071-mail-flows.md) and [ADR-0072](../adr/0072-federated-identity-google-sign-in.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **The step check and the lock** — A step ends green on the step check, `pnpm step:check`, defined beside the gate in `CLAUDE.md` §Commands: `pnpm check`, then `vitest run --changed` against the lane's merge base with `main` on each affected package's integration config — every integration file when the diff touches what the tier is built from, a migration, the harness, an `.env.test`, an integration config or a manifest — `size` only when an SPA is in turbo's `...[<base>]` filter, and `format:check`. A failed file is re-run in its set first; failing there again, or alone, makes it the step's defect, and only one that passes in its set and alone twice is a flake, named in the step's note. A lane ends green on the gate — the whole tree, by CI on every push and on the machine once, at ship. `test`, `test:int`, `size` and `test:e2e` run inside `scripts/with-lock.mjs`, one lock every worktree of a clone shares, which prints its holder while a second lane waits. A cached result is a proof: nothing passes `--force`. — [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) (lanes on one machine and one `main`) as carried by [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md), [ADR-0026](../adr/0026-task-graph-caching-and-serialisation.md) (turborepo task graph) as carried by [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-grid-and-admin-followups.md) and [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md), [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-adr-lifecycle-and-verification.md) (ADR lifecycle v2) as carried by [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md)
- **The first link runs every check** — `lint`'s `dependsOn` carries every root and app check the repository defines — `test:scripts`, `docs:check`, `i18n:check` — and a hygiene case refuses a check it does not name, so a new one joins by predicate. A cached task's restored outputs must not decide its own result: a buildinfo sits under a cached output only beside the emit it belongs to, and a package's `check-types` is uncached — the root table says `cache: false` and the apps opt back in with no output — so no restored buildinfo reaches a package's `tsc -b`. Coverage is reported with no threshold — on every run in the node suites, and in the jsdom suites only on `--coverage`, which keeps the slowest link a quarter shorter; `pnpm audit --prod` runs nightly beside the browser tier, reported and never gating. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups), [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) (backend closing wave) as carried by [ADR-0083](../adr/0083-row-level-security-without-widenings.md)
- **Pinning, holds and the cooldown** — Caret ranges by default and exact for the runtime framework and the compiler; any other exact pin is named with its reason in `renovate.json`'s pinning register. A version many workspaces declare lives in the `catalog:`; GitHub Actions are pinned by digest and the base images carry a named Renovate rule. A dependency held below a version is one `overrides` entry in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, not a pin per workspace. `minimumReleaseAge` is one day for pnpm and for Renovate alike, with the one-install override for a younger security fix written beside pnpm's setting, and a lockfile through review installs under `trustLockfile`. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **The reference images** — Three images from the repository root: the API's runs as `node` with a `HEALTHCHECK` on `/health/live`, and each SPA's runs `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged` as uid 101 on port 8080 with a `HEALTHCHECK` on `/healthz` — `nginx.conf`'s `listen`, the Dockerfile's `EXPOSE` and health check, and the compose mapping name one port. Every build stage copies the lockfile alone and runs `pnpm fetch` before `COPY . .`, then installs `--offline`; no `ARG` sits above the fetch. Every service in `docker/prod/compose.yaml` states a CPU and memory limit and the shared, size-capped `json-file` log driver. — [ADR-0059](../adr/0059-ci-containers-and-deployment.md) (continuous integration, container images and the reference deployment) as carried by [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md), [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) (backend closing wave) as carried by [ADR-0083](../adr/0083-row-level-security-without-widenings.md)
- **The compiler** — `tsc -b` runs TypeScript 7, the catalog's exact version, in every workspace. `typescript-eslint` needs the JavaScript API 7 does not have, so `@repo/eslint-config` alone declares `typescript` as an exact `npm:typescript@6.0.x` alias. The lockfile carries those two versions and no third. The alias, its Renovate hold and the `@typescript-eslint/*>typescript` peer entries go together, with the first `typescript-eslint` whose peer admits 7. Declarations are the native compiler's own — type-equivalent to 6.0's, not byte-identical. — [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) (the native compiler)
- **Forking** — A fork is a clone that keeps history, adds this repository as the `starter` remote and merges from it. A fork never edits an inherited record — it supersedes, because an edit turns the next merge into a conflict and erases which decision was deliberately dropped. `docs/adr/` and `.claude/` are carried into a fork; `docs/plan/` and `docs/CHANGELOG.md` are this repository's journal, reset by `/bootstrap`. The starter merge alone keeps the fork's journal, defining both drivers on its own command line — `git -c merge.ours.driver=true -c merge.union.driver=true merge starter/main` — and then removes every journal file the merge brought, which no attribute keeps out: `git diff --name-only --no-renames --diff-filter=A ORIG_HEAD starter/main -- docs/plan | xargs -r git rm -qf --ignore-unmatch` takes the plans, notes files and lane files the starter added and those the fork deleted that come back as a modify/delete conflict — two commits, never the working tree, so a merge that refuses to start leaves the fork's staged work alone — a conflict on a journal file the fork already had keeps the fork's side, and `docs/upstreaming.md`'s merge-down runs the same commands. Neither driver is defined in a clone's or a global config, so a lane merge conflicts on the ledger and the plans and keeps both sides of the notes and the changelog, which `.gitattributes` puts on `merge=union`. Those two are appended to; their existing text — the changelog's preamble, a notes file's earlier entries — is edited only by the lane that ships. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) and [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md), [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) (lanes on one machine and one `main`) as carried by [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md), [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md) (fork readiness)
- **The bootstrap and the rehearsal** — A fork's journal is reset by a script, `pnpm bootstrap --prefix <name>` (`scripts/bootstrap.mjs`), which the `/bootstrap` skill runs: it removes the starter's plans, notes and lane files and keeps `docs/plan/lanes/README.md`, writes the empty ledger under the fork's prefix with the window section's generated block and no link to the starter's frozen history, resets the changelog to its preamble, and refuses a tree that is not a fresh clone of the starter. A rehearsal, `pnpm test:fork`, uncached in the gate's `test` link and in the step check because it reads the whole tree, bootstraps a temporary clone, merges a simulated starter ship into it with the commands `docs/forking.md` states, and runs the fork's checks, so a change that breaks a fork breaks the starter's gate. A script test never depends on the starter's own journal: what it reads of one is a fixture. On a ledger with no rows, `/scope` writes the first row the operator names. — [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md) (fork readiness), [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) and [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md)
- **Upstreaming** — A generic feature travels back re-implemented as its own deliverable off `starter/main`, never as a cherry-pick: the fork's diff is the specification, not the patch. Generic has a test — no fork domain nouns, and no reference to the fork's own record numbers or plan steps. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) and [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md)
- **Versioning** — `/ship` tags the shipping commit `<prefix>-D<n>` and writes one changelog entry per shipped deliverable — not per commit, and not semver. The prefix is the one `Tag prefix:` line of the ledger's header, which `pnpm docs:check` requires: `starter` in the starter, and the fork's own, never `starter`, once `/bootstrap` writes it, so a fetched starter tag never meets a fork's. Product release tags are `v<version>` and belong to the release tool the releasing repository chooses; the starter adopts none. — [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) (build versions) as carried by [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) and [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md), [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) and [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md)
- **Citations that survive a fork** — In `.claude/**` every record citation carries a topic gloss and never a bare range, and no step numbers or dates appear. Source-code comments keep their step references — they are the reasoning attached to the code that carries it. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) and [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md)
- **The digests** — `docs/rules/<area>.md` states the rules currently in force, each line naming its record; the rule files and the skills load the digest for their area. The records remain the source of truth, and the digest is generated at ship rather than edited. The rule lines live in `scripts/rules-digest.mjs`, and the generator refuses an accepted record that no line cites as its own — accepting a record means writing its lines. — [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-starter-lifecycle.md) (the starter lifecycle) as carried by [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) and [ADR-0082](../adr/0082-lanes-on-one-machine-and-one-main.md) and [ADR-0084](../adr/0084-fork-readiness.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **Specs and notes** — A behaviour spec per capability in `docs/specs/` is current truth, edited in place with the behaviour and carried into forks like code. A plan file holds only what `/step` executes; the build notes go to its `.notes.md` sibling, so a builder opens the plan and one spec rather than the journal. — [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) (behaviour specs, and the plan apart from its notes)
